short: A heavily outnumbered German colonial force repelled a British amphibious assault in German East Africa.
full:
On 3 November 1914, an expeditionary force of the British Indian Army attempted an amphibious landing at the port city of Tanga in German East Africa. The assault was disorganized and poorly executed. They were met by a much smaller defending force of German colonial troops (Schutztruppe) and local askaris commanded by Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, who utilized the dense coastal vegetation for deadly ambushes.

The British forces were completely routed, abandoning vast quantities of modern equipment and supplies as they fled back to their ships. This humiliating defeat at the "Battle of the Bees" fortified Lettow-Vorbeck's position, enabling his forces to sustain a successful guerrilla campaign that tied down hundreds of thousands of Allied troops in Africa for the duration of the war.
